question.worked_solution:
Notice that the terms of the corresponding sequence  

$$
4,\,8,\,16,\,…,\,64,\,128.
$$

  

are powers of $2,$ beginning with ${2}^{2}=4$ and ending with ${2}^{7}=128,$ so there are $6$ terms in total.  

Therefore, the $n$th term of the sequence has the form

$$
{a}_{n}={2}^{n+1},
$$

where $n$ ranges from $n=1$ to $n=6.$ Indeed:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & ={2}^{1+1}=4 \\ {a}_{2} & ={2}^{2+1}=8 \\ {a}_{3} & ={2}^{3+1}=16 \\  & \,\,⋮ \\ {a}_{5} & ={2}^{5+1}=64 \\ {a}_{6} & ={2}^{6+1}=128\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
S=4+8+⋯+64+128={\sum }_{n=1}^{6}{2}^{n+1}.
$$
